notes: Large-unit check on עַד אֲשֶׁר אִם → 'until': every morpheme's sense is inside that one word — עַד the temporal limit, אֲשֶׁר the subordination of the following finite clause, אִם the fixed idiom's particle with no conditional force of its own. Rule 30's one-English-word condition is met, and splitting would leave two morphemes unrepresented beside a rendered one, which rule 30 forbids; the grouping is retained, headed on עַד.

'to go' is a wholly supplied lexical verb: dropping it leaves לִפְנֵי with its whole rendering 'before', so no morpheme is diminished and rule 20 makes it added. The competing reading ('to go before' as the preposition's rendering) is named in the unit note and is handled the same way in v. 20.

'ourselves' stays with the explicit אֲנַחְנוּ rather than with the Niphal: the ASV writes it in emphatic apposition to 'we', not as the object of the passive 'be ... armed'. The competing rule 44 reading, taken in v. 20 where the ASV writes 'arm yourselves', is recorded in the note.

הַמִּבְצָר's article takes the phrase's single fronted 'the' because the rectum is rendered attributively and anarthrously (rules 28, 29), while הָאָרֶץ's is the arthrous case where nothing is fronted.
